x: Tony Whincup has followed his wife to Crewe where they are now settling down. He has joined a local club but is not too happy about it.

Christmas greetings were received from the undermentioned:—Borlase Hendry (Iraq); Norman and Lilian Shrubb (Trinidad and Tobago); Bill Ashford (Iran); Charlie and Doris Smart (Germany); Albert Boddy; Stan Horton; Rodney Stone; Clarice and Bill Merryman; Fred Clay; Dick Towndrow; Rene Howell; Mr. and…
Tony Whincup writes to say that having got over his exam. he is getting down to training. Tony Davis is soldiering at Horsham but says there's not much doing in the way of athletics.

A letter received from Tony Whincup congratulates Gordon Doubleday on being elected as Treasurer in the august ranks of Belgrave officials. Tony has been unable, owing to stomach trouble, to do any running in the Army.

We hope that they will be able to secure leave to run for us during the coming track season, but Harry Greene is not so fortunate as he is now in Benghazi. We have heard from Tony Whincup who is still in Cheshire and doing a good job of work with the lads of the Crewe L.M.R.
Also at this meeting we saw Tony Whincup who had come over from Crewe to see the lads, and Tony was interested to hear about our 20 miles road race and has sent along a cheque to Arthur Whitehead.
That old stalwart TONY WHINCUP has experienced a spell of bad health in recent months, but hopes to overcome his troubles in the near future and show himself again at Wimbledon.

A very cheerful letter has been received from TONY WHINCUP who has not been seen around for a long time. Tony has been incapacitated for some time with nerve-sheath damage to his spine but is now able to get about with the aid of a stick.

TONY WHINCUP found that the flashback photo in the June BELGRAVIAN brought back many memories of fine athletes and administrators. He also recalled that the picture was taken when he was trying to get a boat home from India.
He is now getting back into training and hopes to run on the track next summer. Cheerful letters from ALF TAYLOR and TONY WHINCUP remind us of two stalwarts of years ago.

Tony Whincup died in October aged 75. We hadn't seen a lot of Tony in recent years but, a Belgravian since 1948, he was one of those myriad members who have remained true to his club over a long period.
